notes.overview: 4.909 km, 19 turns, WEC layout. A rhythm circuit that strongly punishes poor kerb use -- GT3 gets unsettled by over-aggressive kerbs, and Hypercars need smoother inputs because kerbs upset aero load. The lap is defined by its named complexes: Tamburello (2-4, a left-right-left sequence), Villeneuve (5-6), Tosa (7), Piratella (blind left, 9), Acque Minerali (11-13), Variante Alta (14-15) and the Rivazza double-left (17-18), linked by flat kinks. Carry rhythm rather than overdriving individual corners; watch throttle management at Tosa and Rivazza. Overusing kerbs and breaking rhythm are the recurring mistakes.

corners.2-4: High-speed left-right-left sequence, braking at the flag-light on the right, focus on balance/positioning; aggressive kerb use is possible for GT3, but Hypercar should prioritize aero stability over attacking the kerb.
corners.5-6: Short braking at the second board on the right, let the car roll through T5 and brake lightly again for T6, flat kerbs are usable, late apex, prepare early for a clean exit into Tosa.
corners.7: Slow uphill hairpin, use all the track width, brake early, late apex, exit traction is critical. Hypercar guide adds smooth throttle is essential to rotate with minimal steering.
corners.9: Blind left-hander, brake at the flag-light on the right, avoid mid-corner steering corrections and running wide on exit.
corners.11-13: Technical downhill complex; brake lightly for T11 and set up left for T12, direction change needs patience with mid-to-late throttle, don't attack the inside kerbs, use all the track on the left; T12 is a subtle, barely-recognisable left kink.
corners.14-15: Aggressive chicane, straight-line braking only, kerbs are strongly cuttable (watch track limits), use all of the exit kerb, exit stability matters more than entry speed.
corners.17-18: Final double left-hander, brake early for T17 (flag-light on the right), mid-apex T17 using all the track and kerb, a slight brake tap for T18, prioritize the exit onto the main straight.
